text.p: The Hyland Division of Baxter Healthcare Corp said on Sunday it was voluntarily recalling from the market three lots of Recombinate Antihemophilic Factor.
The company said it initiated the recall after it noted, during a routine quality assurance test, that four of 10,000 mock units tested were found to contain penicillium, a type of mold.
Prior to that evaluation, samples of the actual recalled lots had previously passed routine sterility and quality assurance testing, the company said.
In addition, the company said there have been no reports of lack of sterility with any lot of Recombinate, including the three recalled.
The company said that it and the Food and Drug Administration will continue to evaluate and monitor the situation.
The company called the recall a "precautionary measure."
The Hyland Division immediately closed the manufacturing area in question, the company said.
The affected area will remain closed until the necessary precautions have been implemented to ensure this will not happen again, the company said.
It is anticipated that this action will have limited impact on the availability of Recombinate and Hyland's other therapeutic proteins, the company said.
Recombinate is a genetically engineered, monoclonally purified concentrate of Factor VIII that is used to treat Hemophilia A.
